newsitem.title: USA: Two die in chemical accident on tanker ship.
newsitem.headline: Two die in chemical accident on tanker ship.

text.p: Two men died on Friday when they were overcome by a toxic chemical being loaded into a tanker ship and fell into the tank.
U.S. Coast Guard Petty Officer Scott Clingenpeel said the bodies of the victims had not yet been retrieved because the tanker was filled with ethylene dichloride, a highly flammable petrochemical.
"They were discovered in the tank of the ship, which would indicate they were overcome by fumes and fell in. I'm sure they died rapidly -- it's a very toxic environment," he said.
Another man was injured in the incident, the cause of which was under investigation, Clingenpeel said.

"There was no explosion...it seems like one of the standard scenarios for an industrial accident. Somewhere along the line something just happened that really wasn't that drastic but it was just enough to get somebody," he said.

All the victims were crewmen on the Formosa Two, which was being loaded with petrochemicals produced at the Taiwanese-owned Formosa Plastics Corp plant in Point Comfort, Texas, about 100 miles (160 km) southwest of Houston.
Clingenpeel said the condition of the injured crewman was not yet known. He said officials were trying to determine how to remove the bodies from the ship without endangering others.
